text:
Situation: Sodium chloride has been on FDA's drug shortage list since 2015-02-17 and remains listed as of 2026-10-21, a duration of 140 months. Current inventory at Corvale East shows sodium chloride 0.9 mg/mL 125 mL syringes at 10.2 days' supply and sodium chloride 9 mg/mL at 9.2 days' supply. Corvale General holds multiple sodium chloride lots ranging from 8.9 to 14.4 days' supply. Corvale Lakeside reports sodium chloride 9 mg/mL at 16.7 days' supply.

Why (FDA record): FDA first posted the sodium chloride shortage on 2015-02-17. Multiple registered plants on our product labels received OAI classifications and warning letters from FDA within three years before the shortage posting. Baxter Healthcare Corporation plants received OAI classifications on 2012-11-16, 2013-01-11, 2013-04-19, 2014-02-11, 2014-03-28, 2015-04-28, 2015-05-01, 2016-02-26, 2016-06-08, and 2016-10-03. Baxter warning letters were issued on 2013-05-31, 2014-10-21, and 2016-08-25. Hospira, Inc. plants received OAI classifications on 2010-01-19, 2011-06-17, 2011-08-04, 2016-06-08, and 2018-08-15, with warning letters on 2010-04-12 and 2017-02-14. Fresenius Kabi USA, LLC plants received OAI classifications on 2011-07-08 and 2013-01-11, with a warning letter on 2012-02-22.

Our position: The prolonged shortage and low days' supply across sites create supply continuity risk. The rule-based best option is Ionis Pharmaceuticals, Inc., which is not on FDA's shortage list today and operates the IONIS PHARMS INC. plant.

Recommended actions:
1. Initiate purchase agreement with Ionis Pharmaceuticals, Inc. — requires approval by Pharmacy Buyer and P&T Committee.
2. Qualify Medefil, Inc., Samson Medical Technologies, L.L.C., Sandoz Inc, and Sportpharm LLC as secondary sources — requires approval by Pharmacy Buyer and Quality Assurance.
3. Establish minimum par levels of 14 days for all sodium chloride presentations at each site — requires approval by Pharmacy Director and Materials Management.
4. Implement weekly inventory review for sodium chloride across Corvale East, General, and Lakeside — requires approval by Pharmacy Operations Manager.

Not recommended: Switching clinical protocols or compounding alternatives; those are clinical decisions for the treating clinicians and the committee.
